analyst.thesis:
What changed since Saturday: the 8/1 tick queued a 42%-of-book E&P rotation (DVN 15% / COP 12% / FANG 10%, CVX to 5%) explicitly built on three legs — a valuation gap vs XOM/CVX's Q2 prints, three dated upstream earnings catalysts inside four sessions, and a firming crude complex on Hormuz tanker-attack risk. That third leg broke today: Trump paused planned strikes on Iran and reopened talks, and Brent gave back roughly 9% of its recent run intraday as 'a hedge against war stops working the moment the war looks negotiable' (TheStreet). This is exactly the concentration risk I named last tick as 'the largest risk I am carrying' — I identified it in the abstract but sized the sleeve as if it wouldn't hit. It hit. The Saturday limits (DVN 45.58, COP 121.68, FANG 204.98, CVX 198.80) did their job in the crash: today's session opened well under every limit (DVN 44.09, COP 117.99, FANG 198.73, CVX 194.71 — Robinhood fundamentals), so the rotation bought into the morning low rather than chasing a gap-up, and DVN/COP have since partially recovered intraday (DVN 44.09->44.40 live, COP 117.99->118.67 live). That's the discipline working as designed. What it doesn't do is protect against being wrong about direction — and OPEC+ ratifying its routine step didn't validate the thesis so much as a much bigger, unmodeled catalyst (a negotiated Hormuz reopening) partially invalidated the physical-supply-risk leg. The valuation gap (DVN 12.5x vs COP 20.5x vs CVX 18.9x vs FANG's impaired 228.8x) and the earnings catalysts (DVN 8/4, COP 8/6, FANG tonight) are real and unaffected by today's headline, so I am not abandoning the sleeve — I am cutting it from 42% to about 21% and letting the reduced size carry the three prints, rather than a full-size bet resting on a premium that just proved reversible inside one session.

Second change: LLY (the standing 14% anchor into its own 8/5 print) drew two pieces of fresh, negative, dated news I did not have Saturday. Trump threatened a 250% tariff on imported pharmaceuticals and sent letters to 17 drugmakers demanding price cuts by September 29 — a real policy overhang independent of the print. And weekly Zepbound prescriptions are reported losing share to Novo Nordisk's Wegovy, a competitive data point, not sentiment. LLY is now 10.3% off a 52-week high set just July 7 — a real, recent pullback, not stale news. I'm cutting LLY from 14% to 8% for the print rather than holding full size into a name that picked up two new, unrelated headwinds two sessions before it reports.

Third: FANG and VRTX both report TONIGHT, after this tick locks in and before I get another look. I'm sizing both at the smaller end (FANG 4%, VRTX 5%) specifically to avoid stacking full-size, same-night earnings risk on top of a day the rest of the book already took a real hit — not a view on either print. PYPL, still the one position with no dated catalyst, gets cut hardest (10%->5%) on my own standing discipline plus a fresh RSI(14) read of 80.8 off the settled 7/31 closes — the most overbought name I hold. Net: cash rises from 23% to roughly 51% of the book. That is a genuine risk-off move, not a rebalancing exercise — nearly every position in the book has live, dated, two-sided uncertainty resolving in the next 48 hours, and the premium that funded the largest bet just proved it can unwind in a single session.

reflection.looking_back: The 8/1 weekend tick queued the full E&P rotation — buy DVN 15% / COP 12% / FANG 10%, add CVX to 5%, exit AMD and XOM — with limits ~1% over the settled 7/31 closes (DVN 45.58, COP 121.68, FANG 204.98, CVX 198.80). Those orders settled at today's 8/3 open, well under every limit (DVN 44.09, COP 117.99, FANG 198.73, CVX 194.71), because the whole complex gapped down at the open on breaking Iran de-escalation news rather than up. The book was carried into the session still showing the pre-rotation holdings (BAC, LLY, PYPL, XOM, CVX, VRTX, AMD) per analyst_memory since the fill happens when this tick's runner executes.
worked: The limit-order discipline worked in reverse of its usual failure mode: because the resting orders were limits, not market-on-open chases, the rotation happened to buy directly into the morning's panic low rather than paying up for a gap, and DVN/COP have partially recovered intraday since (DVN 44.09 open -> 44.40 live, COP 117.99 open -> 118.67 live).
OPEC+'s actual 8/2 decision was the routine, already-priced ~188k-190k bpd September step, exactly what the risk note anticipated as the base case — no surprise, no gap on that specific input.
missed: The concentration risk I named explicitly last tick — 'a single Hormuz de-escalation headline breaks all four positions at once' — is exactly what happened within 48 hours: Trump paused planned strikes on Iran and reopened talks, and Brent gave back roughly 9% of its recent run intraday. I had identified the risk correctly but sized the position (42% of the book on one factor) as if it wouldn't hit rather than as insurance against the scenario I'd already named as my biggest exposure.

LLY picked up two new negative, dated inputs I did not have on 8/1 — Trump's 250% pharma-tariff threat and Zepbound losing weekly-script share to Wegovy — landing two sessions before its own 8/5 print. Not a forecasting miss (the news is from today), but it means the 14% anchor going into today was sized on Saturday's information only.
reflection.adjustment: Cut the energy sleeve from 42% to about 21% of equity (DVN 15%->10%, COP 12%->8%, FANG 10%->4%, CVX held at 5%) and trim LLY 14%->8% on the fresh competitive/tariff overhang into its print, plus PYPL 10%->5% on an RSI(14) of 80.8. Cash rises from 23% to roughly 51%. The process fix: a position sized on a war-risk premium needs an explicit size cap tied to how reversible that premium is, not just a valuation floor — next time I flag a geopolitical risk as 'the largest risk I am carrying,' the sizing has to reflect that language at entry, not just in the risk list.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2025-02-03–2026-08-03, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
